### Steering

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Anatomic_bicycle_grips_made_of_leather.jpg/250px-Anatomic_bicycle_grips_made_of_leather.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anatomic_bicycle_grips_made_of_leather.jpg)

Bicycle grips made of leather. Anatomic shape distributes weight over [palm area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand "Hand") to prevent cyclist's palsy ([ulnar syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulnar_tunnel_syndrome "Ulnar tunnel syndrome")).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-70)

The [handlebars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_handlebar "Bicycle handlebar") connect to the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_(bike) "Stem (bike)") that connects to the fork housing the front wheel. The whole assembly rotates about the steering axis, held by the [headset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headset_(bicycle_part) "Headset (bicycle part)") bearings.

Three styles of handlebar are common. _Upright handlebars_, the norm in Europe and elsewhere until the 1970s, curve gently back towards the rider, offering a natural grip and comfortable upright position. _Drop handlebars_ "drop" as they curve forward and down, allowing the cyclist to use either a more aerodynamic "crouched" position or a more upright position. Mountain bikes generally feature a 'straight handlebar' or 'riser bar' with varying degrees of sweep backward and centimeters rise upwards, as well as wider widths which can provide better handling due to increased leverage against the wheel.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-71)

### Seating

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/San_marco_selle1.jpg/250px-San_marco_selle1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:San_marco_selle1.jpg)

A Selle San Marco saddle designed for women

[Saddles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_saddle "Bicycle saddle") also vary with rider preference, from the cushioned ones favored by short-distance riders to narrower saddles which allow more room for leg swings. Comfort depends on riding position.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-72) With comfort bikes and hybrids, cyclists sit high over the seat, their weight directed down onto the saddle, such that a wider and more cushioned saddle is preferable. For racing bikes where the rider is bent over, weight is more evenly distributed between the handlebars and saddle, the hips are flexed, and a narrower and harder saddle is more efficient. Differing saddle designs exist for male and female cyclists, accommodating the genders' differing anatomies and sit bone width measurements,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-73) although bikes are typically sold with saddles most appropriate for men. Suspension seat posts and seat springs provide comfort by absorbing shock but can add to the overall weight of the bicycle.

A recumbent bicycle has a reclined [chair-like seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_seat "Bicycle seat") that some riders find more comfortable than a saddle, especially riders who suffer from certain types of seat, back, neck, shoulder, or wrist pain. Recumbent bicycles may have either under-seat or over-seat [steering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recumbent_bicycle#Steering "Recumbent bicycle").

### Brakes

Main article: [Bicycle brake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_brake "Bicycle brake")

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Brake.agr-edit.jpg/250px-Brake.agr-edit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brake.agr-edit.jpg)

Linear-pull brake, also known by the [Shimano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimano "Shimano") trademark: V-Brake, on rear wheel of a [mountain bike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_bike "Mountain bike")

Bicycle brakes may be rim brakes, in which friction pads are compressed against the wheel rims; hub brakes, where the mechanism is contained within the wheel hub; or disc brakes, where pads act on a rotor attached to the hub. Most road bicycles use rim brakes, but some use disc brakes.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-74)[Disc brakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disc_brakes "Disc brakes") are more common for mountain bikes, tandems and recumbent bicycles than on other types of bicycles, due to their increased power, coupled with an increased weight and complexity.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-75)

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/BrakeDiskVR.JPG/250px-BrakeDiskVR.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BrakeDiskVR.JPG)

A front disc brake, mounted to the [fork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_fork "Bicycle fork") and hub

With hand-operated brakes, force is applied to brake levers mounted on the handlebars and transmitted via Bowden cables or [hydraulic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydraulic "Hydraulic") lines to the friction pads, which apply pressure to the braking surface, causing friction which slows the bicycle down. A rear hub brake may be either hand-operated or pedal-actuated, as in the back pedal _coaster brakes_ which were popular in North America until the 1960s.

[Track bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_bicycle "Track bicycle") do not have brakes, because all riders ride in the same direction around a track which does not necessitate sharp deceleration. Track riders are still able to slow down because all track bicycles are fixed-gear, meaning that there is no freewheel. Without a freewheel, coasting is impossible, so when the rear wheel is moving, the cranks are moving. To slow down, the rider applies resistance to the pedals, acting as a braking system which can be as effective as a conventional rear wheel brake, but not as effective as a front wheel brake.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-76)

### Suspension

Main article: [Bicycle suspension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_suspension "Bicycle suspension")

Bicycle suspension refers to the system or systems used to _suspend_ the rider and all or part of the bicycle. This serves two purposes: to keep the wheels in continuous contact with the ground, improving control, and to isolate the rider and luggage from jarring due to rough surfaces, improving comfort.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:2-77)

Bicycle suspensions are used primarily on mountain bicycles, but are also common on hybrid bicycles, as they can help deal with problematic vibration from poor surfaces. Suspension is especially important on recumbent bicycles, since while an upright bicycle rider can stand on the pedals to achieve some of the benefits of suspension, a recumbent rider cannot.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:2-77)

Basic mountain bicycles and hybrids usually have front suspension only, whilst more sophisticated ones also have rear suspension. Road bicycles tend to have no suspension.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:2-77)

### Wheels and tires

Main articles: [Bicycle wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_wheel "Bicycle wheel") and [Bicycle tire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_tire "Bicycle tire")

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Cykeld%C3%A4ck_-_Bike_tyres_-_2025.jpg/250px-Cykeld%C3%A4ck_-_Bike_tyres_-_2025.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cykeld%C3%A4ck_-_Bike_tyres_-_2025.jpg)

Two tires of the same make and tread pattern, the lower one completely unused, the upper one has rolled over 1,500 km (900 mi) on varying surfaces.

The wheel axle fits into fork ends in the frame and fork. A pair of wheels may be called a wheelset, especially in the context of ready-built "off the shelf", performance-oriented wheels. Tires vary enormously depending on their intended purpose. [Road bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_bicycles "Road bicycles") typically use tires from 25 mm (1 in) to 35 mm (1.4 in) wide,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-78) sometimes completely smooth, or [slick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slick_tire "Slick tire"), and inflated to high pressure to roll fast on smooth surfaces. Off-road tires are usually wider, from 30 mm (1.2 in) to 100 mm (4 in),[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-79) and have treads for gripping in muddy conditions or metal studs for ice.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-80)

### Accessories

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Loaded_touring_bicycle.JPG/250px-Loaded_touring_bicycle.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Loaded_touring_bicycle.JPG)

Touring bicycle equipped with front and rear [racks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luggage_carrier "Luggage carrier"), fenders (called mud-guards), water bottles in [cages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottle_cage "Bottle cage"), four [panniers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannier "Pannier") and a handlebar bag

Some components, which are often optional accessories on sports bicycles, are standard features on utility bicycles to enhance their usefulness, comfort, safety and visibility. [Fenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_(vehicle) "Fender (vehicle)") with spoilers (mudflaps) protect the cyclist and moving parts from spray when riding through wet areas. In some countries (e.g. Germany, UK), fenders are called mudguards. The [chainguards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainguard "Chainguard") protect clothes from oil on the chain while preventing clothing from being caught between the chain and [crankset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crankset "Crankset") teeth. [Kick stands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick_stand "Kick stand") keep bicycles upright when parked, and [bike locks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike_lock "Bike lock") deter theft. Front-mounted [baskets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_basket "Bicycle basket"), front or rear [luggage carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luggage_carrier "Luggage carrier") or racks, and [panniers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannier "Pannier") mounted above either or both wheels can be used to carry equipment or cargo. Parents sometimes add rear-mounted [child seats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_transport "Baby transport"), an auxiliary saddle fitted to the crossbar, or both to transport children. Bicycles can also be fitted with a hitch to tow a [trailer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_trailer "Bicycle trailer") for carrying cargo, a child, or both.

[Toe-clips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clipless#Clipless_pedals "Clipless"), toestraps and [clipless pedals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clipless_pedals "Clipless pedals") help keep the foot locked in the proper pedal position and enable cyclists to pull and push the pedals. Technical accessories include [cyclocomputers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclocomputer "Cyclocomputer") for measuring speed, distance, heart rate, GPS data etc. Other accessories include [lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_lighting "Bicycle lighting"), reflectors, mirrors, racks, trailers, bags, water bottles and [cages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottle_cage "Bottle cage"), and [bells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_bell "Bicycle bell").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-bicycleuniverse-81) Bicycle lights, reflectors, and helmets are required by law in some geographic regions. It is more common to see bicycles with bottle generators, dynamos, lights, fenders, racks and bells in Europe. Bicyclists also have specialized form fitting and high visibility clothing.

Children's bicycles may be outfitted with cosmetic enhancements such as [bike horns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_horn "Bicycle horn"), streamers, and [spoke beads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spoke_beads "Spoke beads").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-82)[Training wheels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_wheels "Training wheels") are sometimes used when learning to ride, but a dedicated [balance bike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balance_bike "Balance bike") teaches independent riding more effectively.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-84)

[Bicycle helmets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_helmet "Bicycle helmet") can reduce injury in the event of a collision or accident, and a suitable helmet is legally required of riders in many jurisdictions.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-86) Helmets may be classified as an accessory[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-bicycleuniverse-81) or as an item of clothing.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-87)

[Bike trainers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_trainer "Bicycle trainer") are used to enable cyclists to cycle while the bike remains stationary. They are frequently used to warm up before races or indoors when riding conditions are unfavorable.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-88)

### Standards

A number of formal and industry standards exist for bicycle components to help make spare parts exchangeable and to maintain a minimum product safety. The [International Organization for Standardization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Organization_for_Standardization "International Organization for Standardization") (ISO) has a special technical committee for cycles, TC149, that has the scope of "Standardization in the field of cycles, their components and accessories with particular reference to terminology, testing methods and requirements for performance and safety, and interchangeability".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-89)

The [European Committee for Standardization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Committee_for_Standardization "European Committee for Standardization") (CEN) also has a specific Technical Committee, TC333, that defines European standards for cycles. Their mandate states that CEN cycle standards shall harmonize with [ISO standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_standards "List of ISO standards"). Some CEN cycle standards were developed before ISO published their standards, leading to strong European influences in this area. European cycle standards tend to describe minimum safety requirements, while ISO standards have historically harmonized parts geometry.[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-91)

## Industry

This section is an excerpt from [Bicycle industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_industry "Bicycle industry").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bicycle_industry&action=edit)]

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/Geuken_Rijwielen_second-hand_bicycles_on_display%2C_Winschoten_%282020%29_01.jpg/250px-Geuken_Rijwielen_second-hand_bicycles_on_display%2C_Winschoten_%282020%29_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Geuken_Rijwielen_second-hand_bicycles_on_display,_Winschoten_(2020)_01.jpg)

The [bicycle industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_industry "Bicycle industry") or cycling industry can broadly be defined as the [industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry_(economics) "Industry (economics)") concerned with [bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycles "Bicycles") and [cycling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling "Cycling"). It includes at least [bicycle manufacturers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bicycle_manufacturers "List of bicycle manufacturers"), part or component manufacturers, and accessory manufacturers. It can also include [distributors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_(business) "Distribution (business)"), [retailers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retailing "Retailing"), bicycle organizations, bicycle event promoters, and bicycle related service providers.

The global bicycle industry generated sales of $66 billion in 2024.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-92)

### Manufacturing and sales

These paragraphs are an excerpt from [List of bicycle brands and manufacturing companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bicycle_brands_and_manufacturing_companies "List of bicycle brands and manufacturing companies").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_bicycle_brands_and_manufacturing_companies&action=edit)]

Over 100 million bicycles are made each year, the top three manufacturing countries being China, India and Taiwan.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-93) In 2025, the global market size was an estimated $116 billion.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-94)

Many bicycle brands do not manufacture their own product, but rather import and re-brand bikes manufactured by others, sometimes designing the bike, specifying the equipment, and providing quality control. There are also brands that have, at different times, been manufacturers as well as [re-branders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badge_engineering "Badge engineering"): a company with manufacturing capability may market models made by other (overseas) factories, while simultaneously manufacturing bicycles in-house, for example, high-end models.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-95)

## Maintenance and repair

[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Frankfurt%2C_Germany_-_Woolworth_bicycle_accessories.jpg/250px-Frankfurt%2C_Germany_-_Woolworth_bicycle_accessories.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Frankfurt,_Germany_-_Woolworth_bicycle_accessories.jpg)

Bicycle maintenance section in a [Woolworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woolworth_(Europe) "Woolworth (Europe)") in [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt") offering various parts and tools like pumps, lights, bells, handlebar grips, saddles, brakes and inner tubes

A bicycle can be kept in good condition for decades.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:4-54) Like all products with mechanical moving parts, bicycles require regular maintenance and replacement of worn parts. A bicycle is relatively simple compared with a car, so some cyclists choose to do at least part of the maintenance themselves. Some components are easy to manage using relatively simple tools, while other components may require specialist manufacturer-dependent tools.

Many bicycle components are available at several different price/quality points; manufacturers generally try to keep all components on any particular bike at about the same quality level, though at the very cheap end of the market there may be some skimping on less obvious components (e.g. bottom bracket).

*   There are several hundred assisted-service community bicycle organizations worldwide.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-96) At a community bicycle organization, [laypeople](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/layperson#Noun "wikt:layperson") bring in bicycles needing repair or maintenance; volunteers teach them how to do the required steps.
*   Full services are available from [bicycle mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_mechanic "Bicycle mechanic") at [local bike shops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_bike_shop "Local bike shop").
*   In areas where it is available, some cyclists purchase roadside assistance from companies such as the [Better World Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_World_Club "Better World Club") or the [American Automobile Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Automobile_Association "American Automobile Association").

### Maintenance

Keeping the tires correctly inflated can make a noticeable difference as to how the bike feels to ride. Bicycle tires usually have a marking on the sidewall indicating the pressure appropriate for that tire, from 100 to 1,400 kPa (15 to 200 psi).[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-97) Over the longer term, tires wear out, after 1,500 to 5,000 kilometres (900 to 3,000 miles); with punctures often the most visible sign of a worn tire.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-98)

Many community cycling organisations will check brakes and other basic parts for free, or bike shops at low cost.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:3-99) Disc brakes can be cleaned[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-100) but may need professional maintenance, but rim brakes are easier to adjust.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:3-99)

Chains can be washed with soapy water then lightly lubricated, but may need replacing after a couple of years.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-:3-99) Other parts, such as derailleur pivot points, can also be lubricated, but lightly as dirt may stick with too much oil.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-101)

### Repair

Very few bicycle components can actually be repaired; replacement of the failing component is normal practice.

The most common roadside problem is a puncture of the tire's [inner tube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_tube "Inner tube"). A patch kit may be employed to fix the puncture or the tube can be replaced, though the latter solution comes at a greater cost and waste of material.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-Guardian-102) Some brands of tires are much more [puncture-resistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puncture_resistance "Puncture resistance") than others, often incorporating one or more layers of [Kevlar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevlar "Kevlar"); the downside of such tires is that they may be heavier and more difficult to fit and remove.

### Tools

Main article: [Bicycle tools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_tools "Bicycle tools")

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Puncture-repaire-kit.jpg/250px-Puncture-repaire-kit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Puncture-repaire-kit.jpg)

Puncture repair kit with tire levers, [sandpaper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandpaper "Sandpaper") to clean off an area of the [inner tube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_tube "Inner tube") around the puncture, a tube of rubber solution ([vulcanizing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulcanization "Vulcanization") fluid), round and oval patches, a metal grater and piece of chalk to make chalk powder (to dust over excess rubber solution). Kits often also include a wax crayon to mark the puncture location.

There are specialized bicycle tools for use both in the shop and at the roadside. Many cyclists carry tool kits. These may include a tire patch kit (which, in turn, may contain any combination of a [hand pump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_pump "Bicycle pump") or [CO 2 pump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_pump#CO2_Inflators "Bicycle pump"), [tire levers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tire_lever "Tire lever"), spare [tubes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_tube "Inner tube"), self-adhesive patches, or tube-patching material, an adhesive, a piece of sandpaper or a metal grater (for roughening the tube surface to be patched) and sometimes even a block of [French chalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_chalk "French chalk")), [wrenches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrench "Wrench"), [hex keys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hex_key "Hex key"), screwdrivers, and a [chain tool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chain_tool "Chain tool"). Special, thin wrenches are often required for maintaining various screw-fastened parts, specifically, the frequently lubricated ball-bearing "cones".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-103)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-104) There are also cycling-specific [multi-tools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-tool "Multi-tool") that combine many of these implements into a single compact device. More specialized bicycle components may require more complex tools, including proprietary tools specific for a given manufacturer.

## Social and historical aspects

The bicycle has had a considerable effect on human society, in both the cultural and industrial realms.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-105)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike#cite_note-106)

### In daily life

See also: [Cycling infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_infrastructure "Cycling infrastructure") and [History of cycling infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_cycling_infrastructure "History of cycling infrastructure")

Around the turn of the 20th century, bicycles reduced crowding in inner-city tenements by allowing workers to commute from more spacious dwellings in the suburbs. They also reduced dependence on horses. Bicycles allowed people to travel for leisure into the country, since bicycles were three times as energy efficient as walking and three to four times as fast.

**Federico Martín Bahamontes**, born **Alejandro Martín Bahamontes** (Spanish:[[feðeˈɾiko maɾˈtim ba(a)ˈmontes]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); 9 July 1928 – 8 August 2023), was a Spanish professional [road racing cyclist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_racing_cyclist "Road racing cyclist"). He won the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and a total of 11 [Grand Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Tour_(cycling) "Grand Tour (cycling)") stages between 1954 and 1965. He won a total of nine [mountain classifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains") and was the first cyclist to complete a ["career triple"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains#Career_triples "King of the Mountains") by winning the mountain classification in all three Grand Tours. Following his retirement, Bahamontes ran a [bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle "Bicycle") and [motorcycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcycle "Motorcycle") shop and was named the best climber in the history of the Tour de France by a panel organised by _[L'Équipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe")_ in 2013.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Bahamontes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Federico Bahamontes was born on 9 July 1928 in [Santo Domingo-Caudilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santo_Domingo-Caudilla "Santo Domingo-Caudilla"), [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo_(province) "Toledo (province)"), to Julián Martín and Victoria Bahamontes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20121-1) Unlike the usual custom of calling a Spaniard by the first of two surnames, Bahamontes is known by his second; there were too many with the surname Martín in his village so he took up his mother's surname. He was named after his uncle, Federico, who was the head of the family and proclaimed that Bahamontes would be called after him at the baptism in the local church.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) Between 1929 and 1931, his parents had three more children, all girls. Bahamontes attended a school in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") run by nuns, which he did not enjoy.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) In 1936, the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") broke out, but Bahamontes' father, a veteran of the [Cuban War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_War_of_Independence "Cuban War of Independence"), did not fight because he was too old. Along with other civilians in Toledo, however, he was enlisted by Nationalist forces to act as reinforcements as Republican forces closed in on Toledo. He managed to escape this service, but when he returned home, he found soldiers who "called themselves [Communists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism")" and ordered him to open the storehouses on the estate where the family lived. He refused, before running away, and eventually escaping the ensuing manhunt by hiding in a doorway.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201210-3)

The family eventually fled to [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") in July 1936. When the family arrived, the city was held by Republican forces who had withstood an attempted invasion from the Nationalists. In October, however, Nationalist forces decided to lay [siege to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Madrid "Siege of Madrid") and Julián was enlisted into the Republican reserve forces and led a [mule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mule "Mule") team that transported supplies.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201211-4) Meanwhile, Bahamontes, along with his mother and sisters, escaped to the village of [Villarrubia de Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarrubia_de_Santiago "Villarrubia de Santiago") due to the intensifying [air raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike") in Madrid. They were joined by Julián after the war, but the family continued to struggle; as he had been with the Republicans, the losing side, Bahamontes' father received no pension and he was forced to break rocks for road construction in order to earn enough money for the family.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201212-5) The young Bahamontes resorted to [theft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theft "Theft") in order to sustain himself and the family; he would jump into the trailers of lorries from a bridge over a road before filling a bag with food from the trailer. He also dug out live ammunition from civil war trenches to sell as scrap metal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201215-6)

In 1946, at the age of 18, Bahamontes bought his first bike for 150 [pesetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta") (roughly equivalent to £250 or US$342.47 in 2014) in order to transport food illegally between villages. As rationing was in place due to economic ruin, the [black market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_market "Black market") for food flourished.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201217-7) It was during this activity that Bahamontes contracted an unknown disease which he believed to be [typhoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid "Typhoid"). Whilst hiding from the [Civil Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Guard_(Spain) "Civil Guard (Spain)"), who had orders to arrest anyone black marketeering, he stood in stagnant water and was bitten by a mosquito (even though typhoid is not spread via mosquitoes). This led to extreme weight loss, loss of hair and [fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fever "Fever").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201219-8) After being restricted to his house for two months, Bahamontes returned to black marketeering, and competed in his first cycling race after two other black marketeers invited him. On 18 July 1947, he cycled to a nearby village where the race began and, with only a banana and lemon as sustenance, he managed to finish second.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201220%E2%80%9321-9)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Bahamontes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Following victory at his second race, Bahamontes began racing as a full-time [amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur "Amateur"); the prize money from such races was significantly more than the wages of what little work there was.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201223-10) He soon formed a friendship and partnership with another cyclist, Ladislau Soria, who was strong on the flat. Together, they dominated the local races with Soria's brother acting as a manager.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201227-11) In his early years as an amateur, Bahamontes won the Tour of Andalusia and Tour of Cadiz; however, he was called up to 18 months of [National service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_service "National service") in July 1949.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201228-12) It was during this time that he opened up a shop in Toledo renting out bikes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201229-13)

Bahamontes first faced professionals at the 1953 [Vuelta a Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Asturias "Vuelta a Asturias"). The field included some of the strongest cyclists in Spain and teams from Italy and Belgium. Racing as an independent semi-professional, he won the opening stage and eventually finished twenty-first out of sixty-nine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201232-14) He competed in more races in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") and elsewhere in Spain before moving to [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), the wealthiest city in Spain. It was here that he received backing from [Santiago Mostajo Trigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Mostajo_Trigo "Santiago Mostajo Trigo"), a former cyclist and businessman who was a "hugely influential figure" in Spanish cycling.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201233-15)

Due to financial reasons, the [Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "Vuelta a España") did not run between 1951 and 1954, so the [Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volta_a_Catalunya "Volta a Catalunya") was the biggest race in Spain. It was there, in [1953](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya"), that Bahamontes won the [King of the Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains"). The race received coverage in _[Mundo Deportivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundo\_Deportivo "Mundo Deportivo")_, a [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia") sports newspaper, as well as having the support of fourteen sponsors.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201235-16) Teams from across Europe competed, with Bahamontes racing for a team directed by Mostajo and sponsored by Balanzas Berkel, a manufacturer of weighing equipment.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201236-17) He performed above expectations, managing a 146 kilometres (91 mi) solo [breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_(cycling) "Breakaway (cycling)") on stage 8 to secure his mountain classification [jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_jersey "Cycling jersey").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201237%E2%80%9338-18)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg/250px-French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg)

Riders at the start of stage one of the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France")

The director of the Spanish team, [Julián Berrendero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Berrendero "Julián Berrendero"), picked Bahamontes for the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France") in the summer of 1953, with instructions to "try to win it".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201248-19) He initially declined, stating that he did not know French and "had no suitcase", but later accepted the offer with a few weeks to go after discussing with his parents. The Spanish team included [1948 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1948 Vuelta a España") winner [Bernardo Ruiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardo_Ruiz "Bernardo Ruiz"), former national champion [Francisco Masip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Masip "Francisco Masip"), and [1953 Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya") winner [Salvador Botella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Botella "Salvador Botella").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201250-20) The first half of the race was relaxed for Bahamontes, until stage eleven where he broke away from the [peloton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloton "Peloton") and went over the [Col d'Aubisque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_d'Aubisque "Col d'Aubisque") in first place. It was on the [fog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fog "Fog")-covered descent, however, that he crashed, eventually finishing thirty-second.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201252-21) Bahamontes continued to score well in the mountain classifications; he was first over the [Col du Tourmalet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Tourmalet "Col du Tourmalet") and [Col de Peyresourde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Peyresourde "Col de Peyresourde").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201253-22) It was the [Col du Galibier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Galibier "Col du Galibier"), however, that was the most important; Bahamontes rode down [Jean Dotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Dotto "Jean Dotto") to finish the climb in first place, thus winning a 100,000 [franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_franc "French franc") (roughly $250 in 2021) prize as well as mountain points which secured him the mountain classification victory.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201254-23) He finished 25th in the [General classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_classification "General classification").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201255-24)

The next year, Bahamontes competed at the [1955 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1955 Vuelta a España").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201264-25) He gained the nickname _el Gitano_ (the gypsy) when he started to sell bike parts to other riders he had bought from factories in France.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201265-26) The race did not go well for Bahamontes; during stage five, he got a "twisted tendon" in his left knee and had a [limp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limp "Limp") when off the bike. The injury was so serious that a protrusion could be felt on his knee several decades later.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201266-27) As a result, Bahamontes would not achieve another Tour de France mountain classification victory until 1958.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201267-28) After receiving treatment for his injury which reduced the pain and [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation "Inflammation"), Bahamontes continued to race. He won the 1955 Vuelta a Asturias, [Vuelta a los Puertos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A1sica_a_los_Puertos_de_Guadarrama "Clásica a los Puertos de Guadarrama") and a hill climb on [Mont Faron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_Faron "Mont Faron").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201270-29) Despite the success, a medical examination before the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Tour_de_France "1955 Tour de France") prevented him from competing and he was replaced by national champion [Antonio Gelabert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Gelabert "Antonio Gelabert").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201271-30)

He won the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_France "Tour de France") in [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), and won the Tour's [Mountains classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountains_classification_in_the_Tour_de_France "Mountains classification in the Tour de France") (also called the "King of the Mountains") six times (1954, 1958, 1959, 1962, 1963, 1964). He also took second and third places overall in 1963 and 1964 respectively. In total, he won seven Tour stages. He was also second in the [1957 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1957 Vuelta a España"), and won the mountains competition then and the following year, 1958, when he finished 6th. He also won the mountains competition in the [Giro d'Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giro_d'Italia "Giro d'Italia") in [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Giro_d'Italia "1956 Giro d'Italia").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012269%E2%80%93271-31)

In the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), Bahamontes benefited from an early escape on a stage in the [Pyrenees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees"), and then won a mountain [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_time_trial "Individual time trial") to the [Puy-de-Dôme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puy-de-D%C3%B4me_(mountain) "Puy-de-Dôme (mountain)"). Into the Alps, he combined with fellow climber [Charly Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charly_Gaul "Charly Gaul") to extend the lead into [Grenoble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenoble "Grenoble"), and although [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") riders [Henry Anglade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Anglade "Henry Anglade") and [Jacques Anquetil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Anquetil "Jacques Anquetil") cut their deficits, neither made up enough time to threaten Bahamontes' overall lead. He won by just over four minutes from Anglade, and became King of the Mountains too.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006236%E2%80%93244-32)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Federico_Bahamontes_(1960)_(cropped).jpg)

Bahamontes in 1960

In 1960, Bahamontes got no further than the first few days of the Tour, after falling ill.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006245-33) In the [1963 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_Tour_de_France "1963 Tour de France"), Anquetil beat Bahamontes into second place. Bahamontes and Anquetil performed well in the Alps and after stage 16 were only three seconds apart in first and second place respectively. Anquetil was able to stay with Bahamontes, the superior climber, over the steep climb of the [Col de la Forclaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_la_Forclaz "Col de la Forclaz") on the following stage, won by Bahamontes. This allowed Anquetil to use his advantage in the [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_trial "Time trial") to overcome his deficit and claim a fourth Tour victory, while Bahamontes finished second.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006260%E2%80%93264-34) A year later, in the [1964 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Tour_de_France "1964 Tour de France"), Anquetil took his fifth victory and the margin over Bahamontes in third was 4:44; [Raymond Poulidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Poulidor "Raymond Poulidor") took second place. Bahamontes had his sixth King of the Mountains win and two more stage wins (bringing his total Tour de France stage wins to seven).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006264%E2%80%93273-35) His final Tour de France came [in 1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Tour_de_France "1965 Tour de France"), where he abandoned on stage 10, having finished the previous day's stage second to last, 40 minutes down. On his final stage, he made one last attack on the [Col de Portet d'Aspet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Portet_d'Aspet "Col de Portet d'Aspet"), in his own words "to show them [the audience] what they would be missing".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012241%E2%80%93242-36)

## Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Bahamontes&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Retirement")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Bagamontes675.jpg/250px-Bagamontes675.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bagamontes675.jpg)

Bahamontes in his bicycle shop in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") in 2005

Following his retirement, Bahamontes opened a bicycle and motorcycle shop in Toledo and offered to lead visitors through a museum dedicated to his career.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-monde-37)

In 2013, during his 85th birthday that coincided with the [100th edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Tour_de_France "2013 Tour de France") of Le Tour de France, he was named the best climber in the history of the race, ahead of French rider [Richard Virenque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Virenque "Richard Virenque"), by a jury selected by [_L' Équipe_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe") newspaper.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto1-42) Members of the jury included active riders, such as the popular French rider [Thomas Voeckler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Voeckler "Thomas Voeckler"), and others such as five-time winner of the race [Bernard Hinault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Hinault "Bernard Hinault"), as well as the general director of Le Tour de France [Christian Prudhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Prudhomme "Christian Prudhomme").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto-40)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto1-42) The award was given by the French President [François Hollande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Hollande "François Hollande").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto1-42) Also, he has been honoured with the _Premio Nacional Francisco Fernández Ochoa_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-43)

Following the death of [Roger Walkowiak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Walkowiak "Roger Walkowiak") in 2017, Bahamontes became the oldest living Tour de France winner.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-44) Following Bahamontes' death, [1968 Tour winner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Tour_de_France "1968 Tour de France")[Jan Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Janssen "Jan Janssen") took over this position.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-45)

Bahamontes died on 8 August 2023. He was 95 years old.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-monde-37) His home town of Toledo declared two days of mourning following his death.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-46)

**Federico Martín Bahamontes**, born **Alejandro Martín Bahamontes** (Spanish:[[feðeˈɾiko maɾˈtim ba(a)ˈmontes]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); 9 July 1928 – 8 August 2023), was a Spanish professional [road racing cyclist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_racing_cyclist "Road racing cyclist"). He won the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and a total of 11 [Grand Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Tour_(cycling) "Grand Tour (cycling)") stages between 1954 and 1965. He won a total of nine [mountain classifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains") and was the first cyclist to complete a ["career triple"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains#Career_triples "King of the Mountains") by winning the mountain classification in all three Grand Tours. Following his retirement, Bahamontes ran a [bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle "Bicycle") and [motorcycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcycle "Motorcycle") shop and was named the best climber in the history of the Tour de France by a panel organised by _[L'Équipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe")_ in 2013.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Bahamontes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Federico Bahamontes was born on 9 July 1928 in [Santo Domingo-Caudilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santo_Domingo-Caudilla "Santo Domingo-Caudilla"), [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo_(province) "Toledo (province)"), to Julián Martín and Victoria Bahamontes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20121-1) Unlike the usual custom of calling a Spaniard by the first of two surnames, Bahamontes is known by his second; there were too many with the surname Martín in his village so he took up his mother's surname. He was named after his uncle, Federico, who was the head of the family and proclaimed that Bahamontes would be called after him at the baptism in the local church.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) Between 1929 and 1931, his parents had three more children, all girls. Bahamontes attended a school in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") run by nuns, which he did not enjoy.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) In 1936, the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") broke out, but Bahamontes' father, a veteran of the [Cuban War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_War_of_Independence "Cuban War of Independence"), did not fight because he was too old. Along with other civilians in Toledo, however, he was enlisted by Nationalist forces to act as reinforcements as Republican forces closed in on Toledo. He managed to escape this service, but when he returned home, he found soldiers who "called themselves [Communists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism")" and ordered him to open the storehouses on the estate where the family lived. He refused, before running away, and eventually escaping the ensuing manhunt by hiding in a doorway.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201210-3)

The family eventually fled to [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") in July 1936. When the family arrived, the city was held by Republican forces who had withstood an attempted invasion from the Nationalists. In October, however, Nationalist forces decided to lay [siege to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Madrid "Siege of Madrid") and Julián was enlisted into the Republican reserve forces and led a [mule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mule "Mule") team that transported supplies.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201211-4) Meanwhile, Bahamontes, along with his mother and sisters, escaped to the village of [Villarrubia de Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarrubia_de_Santiago "Villarrubia de Santiago") due to the intensifying [air raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike") in Madrid. They were joined by Julián after the war, but the family continued to struggle; as he had been with the Republicans, the losing side, Bahamontes' father received no pension and he was forced to break rocks for road construction in order to earn enough money for the family.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201212-5) The young Bahamontes resorted to [theft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theft "Theft") in order to sustain himself and the family; he would jump into the trailers of lorries from a bridge over a road before filling a bag with food from the trailer. He also dug out live ammunition from civil war trenches to sell as scrap metal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201215-6)

In 1946, at the age of 18, Bahamontes bought his first bike for 150 [pesetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta") (roughly equivalent to £250 or US$342.47 in 2014) in order to transport food illegally between villages. As rationing was in place due to economic ruin, the [black market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_market "Black market") for food flourished.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201217-7) It was during this activity that Bahamontes contracted an unknown disease which he believed to be [typhoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid "Typhoid"). Whilst hiding from the [Civil Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Guard_(Spain) "Civil Guard (Spain)"), who had orders to arrest anyone black marketeering, he stood in stagnant water and was bitten by a mosquito (even though typhoid is not spread via mosquitoes). This led to extreme weight loss, loss of hair and [fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fever "Fever").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201219-8) After being restricted to his house for two months, Bahamontes returned to black marketeering, and competed in his first cycling race after two other black marketeers invited him. On 18 July 1947, he cycled to a nearby village where the race began and, with only a banana and lemon as sustenance, he managed to finish second.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201220%E2%80%9321-9)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Bahamontes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Following victory at his second race, Bahamontes began racing as a full-time [amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur "Amateur"); the prize money from such races was significantly more than the wages of what little work there was.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201223-10) He soon formed a friendship and partnership with another cyclist, Ladislau Soria, who was strong on the flat. Together, they dominated the local races with Soria's brother acting as a manager.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201227-11) In his early years as an amateur, Bahamontes won the Tour of Andalusia and Tour of Cadiz; however, he was called up to 18 months of [National service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_service "National service") in July 1949.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201228-12) It was during this time that he opened up a shop in Toledo renting out bikes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201229-13)

Bahamontes first faced professionals at the 1953 [Vuelta a Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Asturias "Vuelta a Asturias"). The field included some of the strongest cyclists in Spain and teams from Italy and Belgium. Racing as an independent semi-professional, he won the opening stage and eventually finished twenty-first out of sixty-nine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201232-14) He competed in more races in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") and elsewhere in Spain before moving to [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), the wealthiest city in Spain. It was here that he received backing from [Santiago Mostajo Trigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Mostajo_Trigo "Santiago Mostajo Trigo"), a former cyclist and businessman who was a "hugely influential figure" in Spanish cycling.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201233-15)

Due to financial reasons, the [Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "Vuelta a España") did not run between 1951 and 1954, so the [Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volta_a_Catalunya "Volta a Catalunya") was the biggest race in Spain. It was there, in [1953](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya"), that Bahamontes won the [King of the Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains"). The race received coverage in _[Mundo Deportivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundo\_Deportivo "Mundo Deportivo")_, a [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia") sports newspaper, as well as having the support of fourteen sponsors.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201235-16) Teams from across Europe competed, with Bahamontes racing for a team directed by Mostajo and sponsored by Balanzas Berkel, a manufacturer of weighing equipment.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201236-17) He performed above expectations, managing a 146 kilometres (91 mi) solo [breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_(cycling) "Breakaway (cycling)") on stage 8 to secure his mountain classification [jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_jersey "Cycling jersey").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201237%E2%80%9338-18)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg/250px-French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg)

Riders at the start of stage one of the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France")

The director of the Spanish team, [Julián Berrendero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Berrendero "Julián Berrendero"), picked Bahamontes for the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France") in the summer of 1953, with instructions to "try to win it".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201248-19) He initially declined, stating that he did not know French and "had no suitcase", but later accepted the offer with a few weeks to go after discussing with his parents. The Spanish team included [1948 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1948 Vuelta a España") winner [Bernardo Ruiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardo_Ruiz "Bernardo Ruiz"), former national champion [Francisco Masip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Masip "Francisco Masip"), and [1953 Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya") winner [Salvador Botella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Botella "Salvador Botella").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201250-20) The first half of the race was relaxed for Bahamontes, until stage eleven where he broke away from the [peloton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloton "Peloton") and went over the [Col d'Aubisque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_d'Aubisque "Col d'Aubisque") in first place. It was on the [fog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fog "Fog")-covered descent, however, that he crashed, eventually finishing thirty-second.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201252-21) Bahamontes continued to score well in the mountain classifications; he was first over the [Col du Tourmalet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Tourmalet "Col du Tourmalet") and [Col de Peyresourde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Peyresourde "Col de Peyresourde").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201253-22) It was the [Col du Galibier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Galibier "Col du Galibier"), however, that was the most important; Bahamontes rode down [Jean Dotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Dotto "Jean Dotto") to finish the climb in first place, thus winning a 100,000 [franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_franc "French franc") (roughly $250 in 2021) prize as well as mountain points which secured him the mountain classification victory.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201254-23) He finished 25th in the [General classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_classification "General classification").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201255-24)

The next year, Bahamontes competed at the [1955 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1955 Vuelta a España").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201264-25) He gained the nickname _el Gitano_ (the gypsy) when he started to sell bike parts to other riders he had bought from factories in France.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201265-26) The race did not go well for Bahamontes; during stage five, he got a "twisted tendon" in his left knee and had a [limp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limp "Limp") when off the bike. The injury was so serious that a protrusion could be felt on his knee several decades later.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201266-27) As a result, Bahamontes would not achieve another Tour de France mountain classification victory until 1958.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201267-28) After receiving treatment for his injury which reduced the pain and [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation "Inflammation"), Bahamontes continued to race. He won the 1955 Vuelta a Asturias, [Vuelta a los Puertos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A1sica_a_los_Puertos_de_Guadarrama "Clásica a los Puertos de Guadarrama") and a hill climb on [Mont Faron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_Faron "Mont Faron").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201270-29) Despite the success, a medical examination before the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Tour_de_France "1955 Tour de France") prevented him from competing and he was replaced by national champion [Antonio Gelabert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Gelabert "Antonio Gelabert").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201271-30)

He won the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_France "Tour de France") in [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), and won the Tour's [Mountains classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountains_classification_in_the_Tour_de_France "Mountains classification in the Tour de France") (also called the "King of the Mountains") six times (1954, 1958, 1959, 1962, 1963, 1964). He also took second and third places overall in 1963 and 1964 respectively. In total, he won seven Tour stages. He was also second in the [1957 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1957 Vuelta a España"), and won the mountains competition then and the following year, 1958, when he finished 6th. He also won the mountains competition in the [Giro d'Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giro_d'Italia "Giro d'Italia") in [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Giro_d'Italia "1956 Giro d'Italia").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012269%E2%80%93271-31)

In the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), Bahamontes benefited from an early escape on a stage in the [Pyrenees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees"), and then won a mountain [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_time_trial "Individual time trial") to the [Puy-de-Dôme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puy-de-D%C3%B4me_(mountain) "Puy-de-Dôme (mountain)"). Into the Alps, he combined with fellow climber [Charly Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charly_Gaul "Charly Gaul") to extend the lead into [Grenoble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenoble "Grenoble"), and although [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") riders [Henry Anglade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Anglade "Henry Anglade") and [Jacques Anquetil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Anquetil "Jacques Anquetil") cut their deficits, neither made up enough time to threaten Bahamontes' overall lead. He won by just over four minutes from Anglade, and became King of the Mountains too.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006236%E2%80%93244-32)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Federico_Bahamontes_(1960)_(cropped).jpg)

Bahamontes in 1960

In 1960, Bahamontes got no further than the first few days of the Tour, after falling ill.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006245-33) In the [1963 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_Tour_de_France "1963 Tour de France"), Anquetil beat Bahamontes into second place. Bahamontes and Anquetil performed well in the Alps and after stage 16 were only three seconds apart in first and second place respectively. Anquetil was able to stay with Bahamontes, the superior climber, over the steep climb of the [Col de la Forclaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_la_Forclaz "Col de la Forclaz") on the following stage, won by Bahamontes. This allowed Anquetil to use his advantage in the [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_trial "Time trial") to overcome his deficit and claim a fourth Tour victory, while Bahamontes finished second.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006260%E2%80%93264-34) A year later, in the [1964 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Tour_de_France "1964 Tour de France"), Anquetil took his fifth victory and the margin over Bahamontes in third was 4:44; [Raymond Poulidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Poulidor "Raymond Poulidor") took second place. Bahamontes had his sixth King of the Mountains win and two more stage wins (bringing his total Tour de France stage wins to seven).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006264%E2%80%93273-35) His final Tour de France came [in 1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Tour_de_France "1965 Tour de France"), where he abandoned on stage 10, having finished the previous day's stage second to last, 40 minutes down. On his final stage, he made one last attack on the [Col de Portet d'Aspet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Portet_d'Aspet "Col de Portet d'Aspet"), in his own words "to show them [the audience] what they would be missing".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012241%E2%80%93242-36)

## Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Bahamontes&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Retirement")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Bagamontes675.jpg/250px-Bagamontes675.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bagamontes675.jpg)

Bahamontes in his bicycle shop in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") in 2005

Following his retirement, Bahamontes opened a bicycle and motorcycle shop in Toledo and offered to lead visitors through a museum dedicated to his career.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-monde-37)

In 2013, during his 85th birthday that coincided with the [100th edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Tour_de_France "2013 Tour de France") of Le Tour de France, he was named the best climber in the history of the race, ahead of French rider [Richard Virenque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Virenque "Richard Virenque"), by a jury selected by [_L' Équipe_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe") newspaper.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto1-42) Members of the jury included active riders, such as the popular French rider [Thomas Voeckler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Voeckler "Thomas Voeckler"), and others such as five-time winner of the race [Bernard Hinault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Hinault "Bernard Hinault"), as well as the general director of Le Tour de France [Christian Prudhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Prudhomme "Christian Prudhomme").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto-40)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto1-42) The award was given by the French President [François Hollande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Hollande "François Hollande").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-auto1-42) Also, he has been honoured with the _Premio Nacional Francisco Fernández Ochoa_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-43)

Following the death of [Roger Walkowiak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Walkowiak "Roger Walkowiak") in 2017, Bahamontes became the oldest living Tour de France winner.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-44) Following Bahamontes' death, [1968 Tour winner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Tour_de_France "1968 Tour de France")[Jan Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Janssen "Jan Janssen") took over this position.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-45)

Bahamontes died on 8 August 2023. He was 95 years old.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-monde-37) His home town of Toledo declared two days of mourning following his death.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes#cite_note-46)

The **Statue of Federico Martín Bahamontes** is an instance of public art located in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain"), Spain. It consists of a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") statue representing Federico Martín Bahamontes, winner of the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and adoptive son of the city of Toledo.

## History and description

Promoted and funded by the Fundación Soliss, the statue is a work by the Valencian sculptor Javier Molina Gil.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2) It represents Federico Martín Bahamontes, the _Eagle of Toledo_, a celebrated cyclist and Adoptive Son of the City of Toledo.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-3) The bronze base on which the statue stands incorporates a die-cut [coat of arms of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Toledo_(Spain) "Coat of arms of Toledo (Spain)"), featuring the characteristic [double-headed eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_eagle "Double-headed eagle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-4)

Cast in [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze"), it attempts to depict a peak Bahamontes, while riding the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) The statue is slightly bigger in height than real-life Federico Martín Bahamontes (1.90 vs 1.77 m).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) Bahamontes reportedly collaborated with the author in the design of the statue,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) letting the sculptor to obtain accurate biometric data.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-7)

Installed in the Paseo del Miradero, in the centre of the city, it was unveiled on 6 May 2018, during a ceremony attended by Bahamontes himself (aged 89 at the time of the inauguration)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-8) as well as by [Miguel Indurain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Indurain "Miguel Indurain"), [Pedro Delgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Delgado "Pedro Delgado") and [Carlos Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sastre "Carlos Sastre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) Mayor [Milagros Tolón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milagros_Tol%C3%B3n "Milagros Tolón") had reportedly let Bahamontes choose the location for his statue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2)

After a vandal attack, the statue appeared toppled from its base on 28 July 2019, with one broken wheel and other damaged pieces.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-9) It was temporarily removed from the public space. It was reinstated to its original location, with reinforcements, in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-10)
