The **Statue of Federico Martín Bahamontes** is an instance of public art located in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain"), Spain. It consists of a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") statue representing Federico Martín Bahamontes, winner of the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and adoptive son of the city of Toledo.

## History and description

Promoted and funded by the Fundación Soliss, the statue is a work by the Valencian sculptor Javier Molina Gil.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2) It represents Federico Martín Bahamontes, the _Eagle of Toledo_, a celebrated cyclist and Adoptive Son of the City of Toledo.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-3) The bronze base on which the statue stands incorporates a die-cut [coat of arms of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Toledo_(Spain) "Coat of arms of Toledo (Spain)"), featuring the characteristic [double-headed eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_eagle "Double-headed eagle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-4)

Cast in [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze"), it attempts to depict a peak Bahamontes, while riding the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) The statue is slightly bigger in height than real-life Federico Martín Bahamontes (1.90 vs 1.77 m).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) Bahamontes reportedly collaborated with the author in the design of the statue,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) letting the sculptor to obtain accurate biometric data.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-7)

Installed in the Paseo del Miradero, in the centre of the city, it was unveiled on 6 May 2018, during a ceremony attended by Bahamontes himself (aged 89 at the time of the inauguration)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-8) as well as by [Miguel Indurain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Indurain "Miguel Indurain"), [Pedro Delgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Delgado "Pedro Delgado") and [Carlos Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sastre "Carlos Sastre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) Mayor [Milagros Tolón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milagros_Tol%C3%B3n "Milagros Tolón") had reportedly let Bahamontes choose the location for his statue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2)

After a vandal attack, the statue appeared toppled from its base on 28 July 2019, with one broken wheel and other damaged pieces.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-9) It was temporarily removed from the public space. It was reinstated to its original location, with reinforcements, in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes?printable=yes#cite_note-10)

The **Statue of Federico Martín Bahamontes** is an instance of public art located in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain"), Spain. It consists of a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") statue representing Federico Martín Bahamontes, winner of the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and adoptive son of the city of Toledo.

## History and description

Promoted and funded by the Fundación Soliss, the statue is a work by the Valencian sculptor Javier Molina Gil.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-arribas-2) It represents Federico Martín Bahamontes, the _Eagle of Toledo_, a celebrated cyclist and Adoptive Son of the City of Toledo.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-3) The bronze base on which the statue stands incorporates a die-cut [coat of arms of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Toledo_(Spain) "Coat of arms of Toledo (Spain)"), featuring the characteristic [double-headed eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_eagle "Double-headed eagle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-4)

Cast in [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze"), it attempts to depict a peak Bahamontes, while riding the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-eclm-5) The statue is slightly bigger in height than real-life Federico Martín Bahamontes (1.90 vs 1.77 m).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-as-6) Bahamontes reportedly collaborated with the author in the design of the statue,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-as-6) letting the sculptor to obtain accurate biometric data.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-7)

Installed in the Paseo del Miradero, in the centre of the city, it was unveiled on 6 May 2018, during a ceremony attended by Bahamontes himself (aged 89 at the time of the inauguration)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-8) as well as by [Miguel Indurain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Indurain "Miguel Indurain"), [Pedro Delgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Delgado "Pedro Delgado") and [Carlos Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sastre "Carlos Sastre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-eclm-5) Mayor [Milagros Tolón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milagros_Tol%C3%B3n "Milagros Tolón") had reportedly let Bahamontes choose the location for his statue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-arribas-2)

After a vandal attack, the statue appeared toppled from its base on 28 July 2019, with one broken wheel and other damaged pieces.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-9) It was temporarily removed from the public space. It was reinstated to its original location, with reinforcements, in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-10)

The **Statue of Federico Martín Bahamontes** is an instance of public art located in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain"), Spain. It consists of a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") statue representing Federico Martín Bahamontes, winner of the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and adoptive son of the city of Toledo.

## History and description

Promoted and funded by the Fundación Soliss, the statue is a work by the Valencian sculptor Javier Molina Gil.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-arribas-2) It represents Federico Martín Bahamontes, the _Eagle of Toledo_, a celebrated cyclist and Adoptive Son of the City of Toledo.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-3) The bronze base on which the statue stands incorporates a die-cut [coat of arms of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Toledo_(Spain) "Coat of arms of Toledo (Spain)"), featuring the characteristic [double-headed eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_eagle "Double-headed eagle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-4)

Cast in [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze"), it attempts to depict a peak Bahamontes, while riding the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-eclm-5) The statue is slightly bigger in height than real-life Federico Martín Bahamontes (1.90 vs 1.77 m).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-as-6) Bahamontes reportedly collaborated with the author in the design of the statue,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-as-6) letting the sculptor to obtain accurate biometric data.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-7)

Installed in the Paseo del Miradero, in the centre of the city, it was unveiled on 6 May 2018, during a ceremony attended by Bahamontes himself (aged 89 at the time of the inauguration)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-8) as well as by [Miguel Indurain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Indurain "Miguel Indurain"), [Pedro Delgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Delgado "Pedro Delgado") and [Carlos Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sastre "Carlos Sastre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-eclm-5) Mayor [Milagros Tolón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milagros_Tol%C3%B3n "Milagros Tolón") had reportedly let Bahamontes choose the location for his statue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-arribas-2)

After a vandal attack, the statue appeared toppled from its base on 28 July 2019, with one broken wheel and other damaged pieces.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-9) It was temporarily removed from the public space. It was reinstated to its original location, with reinforcements, in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes&section=1#cite_note-10)

**Federico Martín Bahamontes**, born **Alejandro Martín Bahamontes** (Spanish:[[feðeˈɾiko maɾˈtim ba(a)ˈmontes]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); 9 July 1928 – 8 August 2023), was a Spanish professional [road racing cyclist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_racing_cyclist "Road racing cyclist"). He won the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and a total of 11 [Grand Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Tour_(cycling) "Grand Tour (cycling)") stages between 1954 and 1965. He won a total of nine [mountain classifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains") and was the first cyclist to complete a ["career triple"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains#Career_triples "King of the Mountains") by winning the mountain classification in all three Grand Tours. Following his retirement, Bahamontes ran a [bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle "Bicycle") and [motorcycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcycle "Motorcycle") shop and was named the best climber in the history of the Tour de France by a panel organised by _[L'Équipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe")_ in 2013.

## Early life

Federico Bahamontes was born on 9 July 1928 in [Santo Domingo-Caudilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santo_Domingo-Caudilla "Santo Domingo-Caudilla"), [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo_(province) "Toledo (province)"), to Julián Martín and Victoria Bahamontes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20121-1) Unlike the usual custom of calling a Spaniard by the first of two surnames, Bahamontes is known by his second; there were too many with the surname Martín in his village so he took up his mother's surname. He was named after his uncle, Federico, who was the head of the family and proclaimed that Bahamontes would be called after him at the baptism in the local church.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) Between 1929 and 1931, his parents had three more children, all girls. Bahamontes attended a school in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") run by nuns, which he did not enjoy.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) In 1936, the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") broke out, but Bahamontes' father, a veteran of the [Cuban War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_War_of_Independence "Cuban War of Independence"), did not fight because he was too old. Along with other civilians in Toledo, however, he was enlisted by Nationalist forces to act as reinforcements as Republican forces closed in on Toledo. He managed to escape this service, but when he returned home, he found soldiers who "called themselves [Communists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism")" and ordered him to open the storehouses on the estate where the family lived. He refused, before running away, and eventually escaping the ensuing manhunt by hiding in a doorway.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201210-3)

The family eventually fled to [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") in July 1936. When the family arrived, the city was held by Republican forces who had withstood an attempted invasion from the Nationalists. In October, however, Nationalist forces decided to lay [siege to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Madrid "Siege of Madrid") and Julián was enlisted into the Republican reserve forces and led a [mule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mule "Mule") team that transported supplies.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201211-4) Meanwhile, Bahamontes, along with his mother and sisters, escaped to the village of [Villarrubia de Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarrubia_de_Santiago "Villarrubia de Santiago") due to the intensifying [air raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike") in Madrid. They were joined by Julián after the war, but the family continued to struggle; as he had been with the Republicans, the losing side, Bahamontes' father received no pension and he was forced to break rocks for road construction in order to earn enough money for the family.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201212-5) The young Bahamontes resorted to [theft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theft "Theft") in order to sustain himself and the family; he would jump into the trailers of lorries from a bridge over a road before filling a bag with food from the trailer. He also dug out live ammunition from civil war trenches to sell as scrap metal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201215-6)

In 1946, at the age of 18, Bahamontes bought his first bike for 150 [pesetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta") (roughly equivalent to £250 or US$342.47 in 2014) in order to transport food illegally between villages. As rationing was in place due to economic ruin, the [black market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_market "Black market") for food flourished.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201217-7) It was during this activity that Bahamontes contracted an unknown disease which he believed to be [typhoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid "Typhoid"). Whilst hiding from the [Civil Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Guard_(Spain) "Civil Guard (Spain)"), who had orders to arrest anyone black marketeering, he stood in stagnant water and was bitten by a mosquito (even though typhoid is not spread via mosquitoes). This led to extreme weight loss, loss of hair and [fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fever "Fever").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201219-8) After being restricted to his house for two months, Bahamontes returned to black marketeering, and competed in his first cycling race after two other black marketeers invited him. On 18 July 1947, he cycled to a nearby village where the race began and, with only a banana and lemon as sustenance, he managed to finish second.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201220%E2%80%9321-9)

## Career

Following victory at his second race, Bahamontes began racing as a full-time [amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur "Amateur"); the prize money from such races was significantly more than the wages of what little work there was.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201223-10) He soon formed a friendship and partnership with another cyclist, Ladislau Soria, who was strong on the flat. Together, they dominated the local races with Soria's brother acting as a manager.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201227-11) In his early years as an amateur, Bahamontes won the Tour of Andalusia and Tour of Cadiz; however, he was called up to 18 months of [National service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_service "National service") in July 1949.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201228-12) It was during this time that he opened up a shop in Toledo renting out bikes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201229-13)

Bahamontes first faced professionals at the 1953 [Vuelta a Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Asturias "Vuelta a Asturias"). The field included some of the strongest cyclists in Spain and teams from Italy and Belgium. Racing as an independent semi-professional, he won the opening stage and eventually finished twenty-first out of sixty-nine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201232-14) He competed in more races in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") and elsewhere in Spain before moving to [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), the wealthiest city in Spain. It was here that he received backing from [Santiago Mostajo Trigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Mostajo_Trigo "Santiago Mostajo Trigo"), a former cyclist and businessman who was a "hugely influential figure" in Spanish cycling.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201233-15)

Due to financial reasons, the [Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "Vuelta a España") did not run between 1951 and 1954, so the [Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volta_a_Catalunya "Volta a Catalunya") was the biggest race in Spain. It was there, in [1953](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya"), that Bahamontes won the [King of the Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains"). The race received coverage in _[Mundo Deportivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundo\_Deportivo "Mundo Deportivo")_, a [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia") sports newspaper, as well as having the support of fourteen sponsors.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201235-16) Teams from across Europe competed, with Bahamontes racing for a team directed by Mostajo and sponsored by Balanzas Berkel, a manufacturer of weighing equipment.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201236-17) He performed above expectations, managing a 146 kilometres (91 mi) solo [breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_(cycling) "Breakaway (cycling)") on stage 8 to secure his mountain classification [jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_jersey "Cycling jersey").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201237%E2%80%9338-18)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg/250px-French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg)

Riders at the start of stage one of the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France")

The director of the Spanish team, [Julián Berrendero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Berrendero "Julián Berrendero"), picked Bahamontes for the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France") in the summer of 1953, with instructions to "try to win it".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201248-19) He initially declined, stating that he did not know French and "had no suitcase", but later accepted the offer with a few weeks to go after discussing with his parents. The Spanish team included [1948 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1948 Vuelta a España") winner [Bernardo Ruiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardo_Ruiz "Bernardo Ruiz"), former national champion [Francisco Masip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Masip "Francisco Masip"), and [1953 Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya") winner [Salvador Botella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Botella "Salvador Botella").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201250-20) The first half of the race was relaxed for Bahamontes, until stage eleven where he broke away from the [peloton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloton "Peloton") and went over the [Col d'Aubisque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_d'Aubisque "Col d'Aubisque") in first place. It was on the [fog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fog "Fog")-covered descent, however, that he crashed, eventually finishing thirty-second.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201252-21) Bahamontes continued to score well in the mountain classifications; he was first over the [Col du Tourmalet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Tourmalet "Col du Tourmalet") and [Col de Peyresourde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Peyresourde "Col de Peyresourde").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201253-22) It was the [Col du Galibier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Galibier "Col du Galibier"), however, that was the most important; Bahamontes rode down [Jean Dotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Dotto "Jean Dotto") to finish the climb in first place, thus winning a 100,000 [franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_franc "French franc") (roughly $250 in 2021) prize as well as mountain points which secured him the mountain classification victory.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201254-23) He finished 25th in the [General classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_classification "General classification").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201255-24)

The next year, Bahamontes competed at the [1955 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1955 Vuelta a España").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201264-25) He gained the nickname _el Gitano_ (the gypsy) when he started to sell bike parts to other riders he had bought from factories in France.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201265-26) The race did not go well for Bahamontes; during stage five, he got a "twisted tendon" in his left knee and had a [limp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limp "Limp") when off the bike. The injury was so serious that a protrusion could be felt on his knee several decades later.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201266-27) As a result, Bahamontes would not achieve another Tour de France mountain classification victory until 1958.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201267-28) After receiving treatment for his injury which reduced the pain and [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation "Inflammation"), Bahamontes continued to race. He won the 1955 Vuelta a Asturias, [Vuelta a los Puertos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A1sica_a_los_Puertos_de_Guadarrama "Clásica a los Puertos de Guadarrama") and a hill climb on [Mont Faron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_Faron "Mont Faron").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201270-29) Despite the success, a medical examination before the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Tour_de_France "1955 Tour de France") prevented him from competing and he was replaced by national champion [Antonio Gelabert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Gelabert "Antonio Gelabert").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201271-30)

He won the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_France "Tour de France") in [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), and won the Tour's [Mountains classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountains_classification_in_the_Tour_de_France "Mountains classification in the Tour de France") (also called the "King of the Mountains") six times (1954, 1958, 1959, 1962, 1963, 1964). He also took second and third places overall in 1963 and 1964 respectively. In total, he won seven Tour stages. He was also second in the [1957 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1957 Vuelta a España"), and won the mountains competition then and the following year, 1958, when he finished 6th. He also won the mountains competition in the [Giro d'Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giro_d'Italia "Giro d'Italia") in [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Giro_d'Italia "1956 Giro d'Italia").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012269%E2%80%93271-31)

In the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), Bahamontes benefited from an early escape on a stage in the [Pyrenees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees"), and then won a mountain [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_time_trial "Individual time trial") to the [Puy-de-Dôme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puy-de-D%C3%B4me_(mountain) "Puy-de-Dôme (mountain)"). Into the Alps, he combined with fellow climber [Charly Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charly_Gaul "Charly Gaul") to extend the lead into [Grenoble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenoble "Grenoble"), and although [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") riders [Henry Anglade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Anglade "Henry Anglade") and [Jacques Anquetil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Anquetil "Jacques Anquetil") cut their deficits, neither made up enough time to threaten Bahamontes' overall lead. He won by just over four minutes from Anglade, and became King of the Mountains too.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006236%E2%80%93244-32)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Federico_Bahamontes_(1960)_(cropped).jpg)

Bahamontes in 1960

In 1960, Bahamontes got no further than the first few days of the Tour, after falling ill.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006245-33) In the [1963 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_Tour_de_France "1963 Tour de France"), Anquetil beat Bahamontes into second place. Bahamontes and Anquetil performed well in the Alps and after stage 16 were only three seconds apart in first and second place respectively. Anquetil was able to stay with Bahamontes, the superior climber, over the steep climb of the [Col de la Forclaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_la_Forclaz "Col de la Forclaz") on the following stage, won by Bahamontes. This allowed Anquetil to use his advantage in the [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_trial "Time trial") to overcome his deficit and claim a fourth Tour victory, while Bahamontes finished second.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006260%E2%80%93264-34) A year later, in the [1964 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Tour_de_France "1964 Tour de France"), Anquetil took his fifth victory and the margin over Bahamontes in third was 4:44; [Raymond Poulidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Poulidor "Raymond Poulidor") took second place. Bahamontes had his sixth King of the Mountains win and two more stage wins (bringing his total Tour de France stage wins to seven).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006264%E2%80%93273-35) His final Tour de France came [in 1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Tour_de_France "1965 Tour de France"), where he abandoned on stage 10, having finished the previous day's stage second to last, 40 minutes down. On his final stage, he made one last attack on the [Col de Portet d'Aspet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Portet_d'Aspet "Col de Portet d'Aspet"), in his own words "to show them [the audience] what they would be missing".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012241%E2%80%93242-36)

## Retirement

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Bagamontes675.jpg/250px-Bagamontes675.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bagamontes675.jpg)

Bahamontes in his bicycle shop in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") in 2005

Following his retirement, Bahamontes opened a bicycle and motorcycle shop in Toledo and offered to lead visitors through a museum dedicated to his career.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-monde-37)

In 2013, during his 85th birthday that coincided with the [100th edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Tour_de_France "2013 Tour de France") of Le Tour de France, he was named the best climber in the history of the race, ahead of French rider [Richard Virenque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Virenque "Richard Virenque"), by a jury selected by [_L' Équipe_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe") newspaper.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto1-42) Members of the jury included active riders, such as the popular French rider [Thomas Voeckler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Voeckler "Thomas Voeckler"), and others such as five-time winner of the race [Bernard Hinault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Hinault "Bernard Hinault"), as well as the general director of Le Tour de France [Christian Prudhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Prudhomme "Christian Prudhomme").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto-40)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto1-42) The award was given by the French President [François Hollande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Hollande "François Hollande").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto1-42) Also, he has been honoured with the _Premio Nacional Francisco Fernández Ochoa_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-43)

Following the death of [Roger Walkowiak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Walkowiak "Roger Walkowiak") in 2017, Bahamontes became the oldest living Tour de France winner.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-44) Following Bahamontes' death, [1968 Tour winner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Tour_de_France "1968 Tour de France")[Jan Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Janssen "Jan Janssen") took over this position.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-45)

Bahamontes died on 8 August 2023. He was 95 years old.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-monde-37) His home town of Toledo declared two days of mourning following his death.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-46)

**Federico Martín Bahamontes**, born **Alejandro Martín Bahamontes** (Spanish:[[feðeˈɾiko maɾˈtim ba(a)ˈmontes]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); 9 July 1928 – 8 August 2023), was a Spanish professional [road racing cyclist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_racing_cyclist "Road racing cyclist"). He won the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and a total of 11 [Grand Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Tour_(cycling) "Grand Tour (cycling)") stages between 1954 and 1965. He won a total of nine [mountain classifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains") and was the first cyclist to complete a ["career triple"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains#Career_triples "King of the Mountains") by winning the mountain classification in all three Grand Tours. Following his retirement, Bahamontes ran a [bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle "Bicycle") and [motorcycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcycle "Motorcycle") shop and was named the best climber in the history of the Tour de France by a panel organised by _[L'Équipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe")_ in 2013.

## Early life

Federico Bahamontes was born on 9 July 1928 in [Santo Domingo-Caudilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santo_Domingo-Caudilla "Santo Domingo-Caudilla"), [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo_(province) "Toledo (province)"), to Julián Martín and Victoria Bahamontes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20121-1) Unlike the usual custom of calling a Spaniard by the first of two surnames, Bahamontes is known by his second; there were too many with the surname Martín in his village so he took up his mother's surname. He was named after his uncle, Federico, who was the head of the family and proclaimed that Bahamontes would be called after him at the baptism in the local church.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) Between 1929 and 1931, his parents had three more children, all girls. Bahamontes attended a school in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") run by nuns, which he did not enjoy.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham20124-2) In 1936, the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") broke out, but Bahamontes' father, a veteran of the [Cuban War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_War_of_Independence "Cuban War of Independence"), did not fight because he was too old. Along with other civilians in Toledo, however, he was enlisted by Nationalist forces to act as reinforcements as Republican forces closed in on Toledo. He managed to escape this service, but when he returned home, he found soldiers who "called themselves [Communists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism")" and ordered him to open the storehouses on the estate where the family lived. He refused, before running away, and eventually escaping the ensuing manhunt by hiding in a doorway.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201210-3)

The family eventually fled to [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") in July 1936. When the family arrived, the city was held by Republican forces who had withstood an attempted invasion from the Nationalists. In October, however, Nationalist forces decided to lay [siege to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Madrid "Siege of Madrid") and Julián was enlisted into the Republican reserve forces and led a [mule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mule "Mule") team that transported supplies.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201211-4) Meanwhile, Bahamontes, along with his mother and sisters, escaped to the village of [Villarrubia de Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarrubia_de_Santiago "Villarrubia de Santiago") due to the intensifying [air raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike") in Madrid. They were joined by Julián after the war, but the family continued to struggle; as he had been with the Republicans, the losing side, Bahamontes' father received no pension and he was forced to break rocks for road construction in order to earn enough money for the family.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201212-5) The young Bahamontes resorted to [theft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theft "Theft") in order to sustain himself and the family; he would jump into the trailers of lorries from a bridge over a road before filling a bag with food from the trailer. He also dug out live ammunition from civil war trenches to sell as scrap metal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201215-6)

In 1946, at the age of 18, Bahamontes bought his first bike for 150 [pesetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta") (roughly equivalent to £250 or US$342.47 in 2014) in order to transport food illegally between villages. As rationing was in place due to economic ruin, the [black market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_market "Black market") for food flourished.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201217-7) It was during this activity that Bahamontes contracted an unknown disease which he believed to be [typhoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid "Typhoid"). Whilst hiding from the [Civil Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Guard_(Spain) "Civil Guard (Spain)"), who had orders to arrest anyone black marketeering, he stood in stagnant water and was bitten by a mosquito (even though typhoid is not spread via mosquitoes). This led to extreme weight loss, loss of hair and [fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fever "Fever").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201219-8) After being restricted to his house for two months, Bahamontes returned to black marketeering, and competed in his first cycling race after two other black marketeers invited him. On 18 July 1947, he cycled to a nearby village where the race began and, with only a banana and lemon as sustenance, he managed to finish second.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201220%E2%80%9321-9)

## Career

Following victory at his second race, Bahamontes began racing as a full-time [amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur "Amateur"); the prize money from such races was significantly more than the wages of what little work there was.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201223-10) He soon formed a friendship and partnership with another cyclist, Ladislau Soria, who was strong on the flat. Together, they dominated the local races with Soria's brother acting as a manager.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201227-11) In his early years as an amateur, Bahamontes won the Tour of Andalusia and Tour of Cadiz; however, he was called up to 18 months of [National service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_service "National service") in July 1949.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201228-12) It was during this time that he opened up a shop in Toledo renting out bikes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201229-13)

Bahamontes first faced professionals at the 1953 [Vuelta a Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Asturias "Vuelta a Asturias"). The field included some of the strongest cyclists in Spain and teams from Italy and Belgium. Racing as an independent semi-professional, he won the opening stage and eventually finished twenty-first out of sixty-nine.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201232-14) He competed in more races in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") and elsewhere in Spain before moving to [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), the wealthiest city in Spain. It was here that he received backing from [Santiago Mostajo Trigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Mostajo_Trigo "Santiago Mostajo Trigo"), a former cyclist and businessman who was a "hugely influential figure" in Spanish cycling.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201233-15)

Due to financial reasons, the [Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "Vuelta a España") did not run between 1951 and 1954, so the [Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volta_a_Catalunya "Volta a Catalunya") was the biggest race in Spain. It was there, in [1953](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya"), that Bahamontes won the [King of the Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Mountains "King of the Mountains"). The race received coverage in _[Mundo Deportivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundo\_Deportivo "Mundo Deportivo")_, a [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia") sports newspaper, as well as having the support of fourteen sponsors.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201235-16) Teams from across Europe competed, with Bahamontes racing for a team directed by Mostajo and sponsored by Balanzas Berkel, a manufacturer of weighing equipment.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201236-17) He performed above expectations, managing a 146 kilometres (91 mi) solo [breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_(cycling) "Breakaway (cycling)") on stage 8 to secure his mountain classification [jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_jersey "Cycling jersey").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201237%E2%80%9338-18)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg/250px-French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:French_team_at_the_start_of_the_Tour_de_France_1954.jpg)

Riders at the start of stage one of the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France")

The director of the Spanish team, [Julián Berrendero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Berrendero "Julián Berrendero"), picked Bahamontes for the [1954 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Tour_de_France "1954 Tour de France") in the summer of 1953, with instructions to "try to win it".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201248-19) He initially declined, stating that he did not know French and "had no suitcase", but later accepted the offer with a few weeks to go after discussing with his parents. The Spanish team included [1948 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1948 Vuelta a España") winner [Bernardo Ruiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardo_Ruiz "Bernardo Ruiz"), former national champion [Francisco Masip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Masip "Francisco Masip"), and [1953 Volta a Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Volta_a_Catalunya "1953 Volta a Catalunya") winner [Salvador Botella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Botella "Salvador Botella").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201250-20) The first half of the race was relaxed for Bahamontes, until stage eleven where he broke away from the [peloton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloton "Peloton") and went over the [Col d'Aubisque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_d'Aubisque "Col d'Aubisque") in first place. It was on the [fog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fog "Fog")-covered descent, however, that he crashed, eventually finishing thirty-second.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201252-21) Bahamontes continued to score well in the mountain classifications; he was first over the [Col du Tourmalet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Tourmalet "Col du Tourmalet") and [Col de Peyresourde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Peyresourde "Col de Peyresourde").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201253-22) It was the [Col du Galibier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_du_Galibier "Col du Galibier"), however, that was the most important; Bahamontes rode down [Jean Dotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Dotto "Jean Dotto") to finish the climb in first place, thus winning a 100,000 [franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_franc "French franc") (roughly $250 in 2021) prize as well as mountain points which secured him the mountain classification victory.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201254-23) He finished 25th in the [General classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_classification "General classification").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201255-24)

The next year, Bahamontes competed at the [1955 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1955 Vuelta a España").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201264-25) He gained the nickname _el Gitano_ (the gypsy) when he started to sell bike parts to other riders he had bought from factories in France.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201265-26) The race did not go well for Bahamontes; during stage five, he got a "twisted tendon" in his left knee and had a [limp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limp "Limp") when off the bike. The injury was so serious that a protrusion could be felt on his knee several decades later.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201266-27) As a result, Bahamontes would not achieve another Tour de France mountain classification victory until 1958.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201267-28) After receiving treatment for his injury which reduced the pain and [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation "Inflammation"), Bahamontes continued to race. He won the 1955 Vuelta a Asturias, [Vuelta a los Puertos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A1sica_a_los_Puertos_de_Guadarrama "Clásica a los Puertos de Guadarrama") and a hill climb on [Mont Faron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_Faron "Mont Faron").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201270-29) Despite the success, a medical examination before the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Tour_de_France "1955 Tour de France") prevented him from competing and he was replaced by national champion [Antonio Gelabert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Gelabert "Antonio Gelabert").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham201271-30)

He won the [Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_France "Tour de France") in [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), and won the Tour's [Mountains classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountains_classification_in_the_Tour_de_France "Mountains classification in the Tour de France") (also called the "King of the Mountains") six times (1954, 1958, 1959, 1962, 1963, 1964). He also took second and third places overall in 1963 and 1964 respectively. In total, he won seven Tour stages. He was also second in the [1957 Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1957 Vuelta a España"), and won the mountains competition then and the following year, 1958, when he finished 6th. He also won the mountains competition in the [Giro d'Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giro_d'Italia "Giro d'Italia") in [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Giro_d'Italia "1956 Giro d'Italia").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012269%E2%80%93271-31)

In the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France"), Bahamontes benefited from an early escape on a stage in the [Pyrenees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees"), and then won a mountain [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_time_trial "Individual time trial") to the [Puy-de-Dôme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puy-de-D%C3%B4me_(mountain) "Puy-de-Dôme (mountain)"). Into the Alps, he combined with fellow climber [Charly Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charly_Gaul "Charly Gaul") to extend the lead into [Grenoble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenoble "Grenoble"), and although [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") riders [Henry Anglade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Anglade "Henry Anglade") and [Jacques Anquetil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Anquetil "Jacques Anquetil") cut their deficits, neither made up enough time to threaten Bahamontes' overall lead. He won by just over four minutes from Anglade, and became King of the Mountains too.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006236%E2%80%93244-32)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Federico_Bahamontes_%281960%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Federico_Bahamontes_(1960)_(cropped).jpg)

Bahamontes in 1960

In 1960, Bahamontes got no further than the first few days of the Tour, after falling ill.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006245-33) In the [1963 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_Tour_de_France "1963 Tour de France"), Anquetil beat Bahamontes into second place. Bahamontes and Anquetil performed well in the Alps and after stage 16 were only three seconds apart in first and second place respectively. Anquetil was able to stay with Bahamontes, the superior climber, over the steep climb of the [Col de la Forclaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_la_Forclaz "Col de la Forclaz") on the following stage, won by Bahamontes. This allowed Anquetil to use his advantage in the [time trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_trial "Time trial") to overcome his deficit and claim a fourth Tour victory, while Bahamontes finished second.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006260%E2%80%93264-34) A year later, in the [1964 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Tour_de_France "1964 Tour de France"), Anquetil took his fifth victory and the margin over Bahamontes in third was 4:44; [Raymond Poulidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Poulidor "Raymond Poulidor") took second place. Bahamontes had his sixth King of the Mountains win and two more stage wins (bringing his total Tour de France stage wins to seven).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGannMcGann2006264%E2%80%93273-35) His final Tour de France came [in 1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Tour_de_France "1965 Tour de France"), where he abandoned on stage 10, having finished the previous day's stage second to last, 40 minutes down. On his final stage, he made one last attack on the [Col de Portet d'Aspet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_de_Portet_d'Aspet "Col de Portet d'Aspet"), in his own words "to show them [the audience] what they would be missing".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFotheringham2012241%E2%80%93242-36)

## Retirement

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Bagamontes675.jpg/250px-Bagamontes675.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bagamontes675.jpg)

Bahamontes in his bicycle shop in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain") in 2005

Following his retirement, Bahamontes opened a bicycle and motorcycle shop in Toledo and offered to lead visitors through a museum dedicated to his career.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-monde-37)

In 2013, during his 85th birthday that coincided with the [100th edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Tour_de_France "2013 Tour de France") of Le Tour de France, he was named the best climber in the history of the race, ahead of French rider [Richard Virenque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Virenque "Richard Virenque"), by a jury selected by [_L' Équipe_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'%C3%89quipe "L'Équipe") newspaper.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto1-42) Members of the jury included active riders, such as the popular French rider [Thomas Voeckler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Voeckler "Thomas Voeckler"), and others such as five-time winner of the race [Bernard Hinault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Hinault "Bernard Hinault"), as well as the general director of Le Tour de France [Christian Prudhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Prudhomme "Christian Prudhomme").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto-40)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto1-42) The award was given by the French President [François Hollande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Hollande "François Hollande").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-auto1-42) Also, he has been honoured with the _Premio Nacional Francisco Fernández Ochoa_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-43)

Following the death of [Roger Walkowiak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Walkowiak "Roger Walkowiak") in 2017, Bahamontes became the oldest living Tour de France winner.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-44) Following Bahamontes' death, [1968 Tour winner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Tour_de_France "1968 Tour de France")[Jan Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Janssen "Jan Janssen") took over this position.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-45)

Bahamontes died on 8 August 2023. He was 95 years old.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-monde-37) His home town of Toledo declared two days of mourning following his death.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-46)

The **Statue of Federico Martín Bahamontes** is an instance of public art located in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain"), Spain. It consists of a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") statue representing Federico Martín Bahamontes, winner of the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and adoptive son of the city of Toledo.

## History and description

Promoted and funded by the Fundación Soliss, the statue is a work by the Valencian sculptor Javier Molina Gil.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2) It represents Federico Martín Bahamontes, the _Eagle of Toledo_, a celebrated cyclist and Adoptive Son of the City of Toledo.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-3) The bronze base on which the statue stands incorporates a die-cut [coat of arms of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Toledo_(Spain) "Coat of arms of Toledo (Spain)"), featuring the characteristic [double-headed eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_eagle "Double-headed eagle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-4)

Cast in [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze"), it attempts to depict a peak Bahamontes, while riding the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) The statue is slightly bigger in height than real-life Federico Martín Bahamontes (1.90 vs 1.77 m).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) Bahamontes reportedly collaborated with the author in the design of the statue,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) letting the sculptor to obtain accurate biometric data.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-7)

Installed in the Paseo del Miradero, in the centre of the city, it was unveiled on 6 May 2018, during a ceremony attended by Bahamontes himself (aged 89 at the time of the inauguration)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-8) as well as by [Miguel Indurain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Indurain "Miguel Indurain"), [Pedro Delgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Delgado "Pedro Delgado") and [Carlos Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sastre "Carlos Sastre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) Mayor [Milagros Tolón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milagros_Tol%C3%B3n "Milagros Tolón") had reportedly let Bahamontes choose the location for his statue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2)

After a vandal attack, the statue appeared toppled from its base on 28 July 2019, with one broken wheel and other damaged pieces.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-9) It was temporarily removed from the public space. It was reinstated to its original location, with reinforcements, in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-10)

The **Statue of Federico Martín Bahamontes** is an instance of public art located in [Toledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toledo,_Spain "Toledo, Spain"), Spain. It consists of a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze") statue representing Federico Martín Bahamontes, winner of the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France") and adoptive son of the city of Toledo.

## History and description

Promoted and funded by the Fundación Soliss, the statue is a work by the Valencian sculptor Javier Molina Gil.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2) It represents Federico Martín Bahamontes, the _Eagle of Toledo_, a celebrated cyclist and Adoptive Son of the City of Toledo.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-3) The bronze base on which the statue stands incorporates a die-cut [coat of arms of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Toledo_(Spain) "Coat of arms of Toledo (Spain)"), featuring the characteristic [double-headed eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_eagle "Double-headed eagle").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-4)

Cast in [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze"), it attempts to depict a peak Bahamontes, while riding the [1959 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Tour_de_France "1959 Tour de France").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) The statue is slightly bigger in height than real-life Federico Martín Bahamontes (1.90 vs 1.77 m).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) Bahamontes reportedly collaborated with the author in the design of the statue,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-as-6) letting the sculptor to obtain accurate biometric data.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-7)

Installed in the Paseo del Miradero, in the centre of the city, it was unveiled on 6 May 2018, during a ceremony attended by Bahamontes himself (aged 89 at the time of the inauguration)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-8) as well as by [Miguel Indurain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Indurain "Miguel Indurain"), [Pedro Delgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Delgado "Pedro Delgado") and [Carlos Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sastre "Carlos Sastre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-eclm-5) Mayor [Milagros Tolón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milagros_Tol%C3%B3n "Milagros Tolón") had reportedly let Bahamontes choose the location for his statue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-arribas-2)

After a vandal attack, the statue appeared toppled from its base on 28 July 2019, with one broken wheel and other damaged pieces.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-9) It was temporarily removed from the public space. It was reinstated to its original location, with reinforcements, in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Statue_of_Federico_Mart%C3%ADn_Bahamontes&printable=yes#cite_note-10)

**Pedro Delgado Robledo** (pronounced[[ˈpeðɾo ðelˈɣaðo roˈβleðo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); born 15 April 1960), also known as **Perico** ([[peˈɾiko]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")), is a Spanish former professional [road bicycle racer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_bicycle_racer "Road bicycle racer"). He won the [1988 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Tour_de_France "1988 Tour de France"), as well as the [Vuelta a España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "Vuelta a España") in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1985 Vuelta a España") and [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Vuelta_a_Espa%C3%B1a "1989 Vuelta a España"). He finished in the top 10 of eighteen [Grand Tours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Tour_(cycling) "Grand Tour (cycling)").

Delgado tested positive for the known masking agent [Probenecid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probenecid "Probenecid") during the [1988 tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Tour_de_France "1988 Tour de France"). The drug, which had been placed on the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee")'s list of banned substances in January of that year, had not yet been banned by the sport's governing body, the [Union Cycliste Internationale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Cycliste_Internationale "Union Cycliste Internationale"); as a consequence, Delgado was allowed to continue racing and was not charged with any doping offence.

Since 1995, he works as a sports commentator for [Televisión Española](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Televisi%C3%B3n_Espa%C3%B1ola "Televisión Española") during important cycling events, first along with journalist Pedro González, and, after his death in January 2000, with Carlos de Andrés.
